newsitem.title: CHILE: Outokumpu in Chile mine talks - report.
newsitem.headline: Outokumpu in Chile mine talks - report.

text.p: Finnish mining company Outokumpu is in talks with Chile's Luksic group to develop the Los Pelambres copper mine, reported newspaper El Diario.
El Diario, quoting sources in the Chilean group, said Luksic executives travelled to Finland last month for discussions with Outokumpu officials.
Neither company was immediately available for comment.
The mine's owners have also been reported to be in talks with two Japanese firms, Nippon Mining and Mitsubishi.
Minera Anaconda, the mining wing of the industrial group, plans to boost production at the pit to 230,000 tonnes a year by late 1998 from 23,000 tonnes last year.
The expansion will cost around $1 billion.
Outokumpu already operates the 125,000-tonne Zaldivar copper pit in Chile and is carrying out studies on its Relincho and Santa Catalina properties in the northern Atacama Desert.
